task: Simplify the DAQ connection strategy to a minimal Wi‑Fi UDP bridge and ensure telemetry flows from Teensy -> ESP32 -> DAQ, and DAQ commands flow from DAQ -> ESP32 -> Teensy.
goal: Use the simplest stable architecture: DAQ and ESP32 talk over UDP on Wi‑Fi; ESP32 and Teensy talk over UART; no extra protocol layers, no duplicate command paths, no simulated telemetry.

architecture.daq_to_esp32: UDP JSON over Wi‑Fi to ESP32 IP 10.0.2.245:4210
architecture.esp32_to_daq: UDP JSON telemetry packet back to the GUI

rules: Do not keep demo or simulation telemetry paths active in live UDP mode.
Do not rely on mDNS as the primary connection method for Windows. Use direct IP fallback and only optional mDNS discovery.
Use JSON only for DAQ <-> ESP32 commands and telemetry.
Keep the protocol very small and consistent.
On the ESP32, store the DAQ IP and port when the first UDP packet arrives.
When DAQ sends DAQ_START, ESP32 immediately forwards DAQ_START to Teensy over UART.
When Teensy sends telemetry, ESP32 parses it and forwards JSON back to the DAQ over UDP.
When DAQ sends STOP, ESP32 forwards STOP to Teensy and stops telemetry.
If no telemetry arrives, do not keep forcing ERROR state in the GUI; keep the socket connected and wait for the next packet.
Use the exact file structure and names already present in this project.

expected_behavior.daq_connect: The DAQ connects to ESP32 over UDP and sends HELLO.
expected_behavior.esp32_handshake: ESP32 replies with ACK/READY state and remembers DAQ client IP and port.
expected_behavior.daq_start: The DAQ sends {"type":"DAQ_START"}. The ESP32 forwards the same message to the Teensy over UART.
expected_behavior.teensy_start: The Teensy accepts one of START_COMMAND values and transitions to RUNNING state.
expected_behavior.teensy_telemetry: The Teensy generates TLM|... lines at 60 Hz while RUNNING.
expected_behavior.esp32_forward: ESP32 reads Serial1, parses TLM|..., builds JSON telemetry, and sends it back to the DAQ over UDP.
expected_behavior.daq_gauges: The DAQ parses the telemetry JSON and updates the gauges. If no packet arrives within 2.0 seconds, it marks timeout only for the UI, not as a network failure.
expected_behavior.daq_stop: The DAQ sends {"type":"STOP"}; ESP32 forwards STOP and Teensy stops telemetry.

changes: Keep the direct IP fallback to 10.0.2.245:4210.
Only auto-send DAQ_START after a real socket connection succeeds, once.
Do not auto-trigger demo data while the real UDP mode is active.
Do not set the DAQ to ERROR just because no telemetry packet arrived in the first 2 seconds while waiting for the system to start; leave it connected and show a timeout state only.
For received JSON telemetry, normalize the fields using keys like rpm, throttle, fuel, cht, egt, vib_x, vib_y, vib_z.
Keep UDP socket creation and receive loop simple and reliable.
Accept both command names and packet types: HELLO, HELLO, DAQ_START, STOP, STATUS, TELEMETRY.
Ignore case differences for message_type.
Emit telemetryReceived only for the actual telemetry packet type.
Do not parse or send unrelated profile or demo packets in live mode.
On UDP packet receive, parse the JSON and read type or command.
If type is HELLO or PING: reply {"type":"ACK","state":"READY"} and keep the DAQ client address.
If type is DAQ_START: forward the command to the Teensy over Serial1 and reply ACK/RUNNING.
If type is STOP: forward STOP to Teensy and reply ACK/STOPPED.
If type is STATUS: reply {"type":"STATUS","state":"READY"}.
If packet is telemetry from Teensy UART, the ESP32 must wrap it into JSON and send it back to the DAQ.
Start Serial1 with TEENSY_UART_BAUD, SERIAL_8N1, TEENSY_RX_PIN=7, TEENSY_TX_PIN=8.
Read lines from Serial1 on every loop.
Accept both TLM|... and TELEMETRY|... messages.
Parse keys exactly as: rpm, load1, load2, temp1, temp2, vibx, viby, vibz.
Build a JSON object like {"type":"TELEMETRY","state":"RUNNING","data":{...}} and send it to the DAQ over UDP via udpSendJson().
Ignore ACK and STATUS messages from the Teensy unless you intentionally want them for logs.
Confirm WiFi SSID and password are correct.
Keep UDP_PORT 4210.
Keep MDNS name engine-daq for optional discovery only.
Keep UART pins TEENSY_RX_PIN 7 and TEENSY_TX_PIN 8.
Keep DEBUG_MODE enabled for serial debugging.
Set default state to STATE_READY during boot so the first DAQ_START can transition to RUNNING.
Process Serial and Serial1 commands together.
Accept START_COMMAND when state is IDLE, READY, or STOPPED.
When START_COMMAND is received: set gDaqState = STATE_RUNNING and reply ACK|state=RUNNING.
When STOP_COMMAND is received: set gDaqState = STATE_STOPPED and reply ACK|state=STOPPED.
When gDaqState == STATE_RUNNING, generate TLM|... telemetry each 1000/60 ms and send it over Serial1.
Keep the message format simple: TLM|rpm=...|load1=...|load2=...|temp1=...|temp2=...|vibx=...|viby=...|vibz=...
Keep START_COMMAND = "DAQ_START" and STOP_COMMAND = "STOP".
Keep PING_COMMAND = "PING" and STATUS_COMMAND = "GET_STATUS".

implementation_order: Update the Teensy state machine and telemetry generation first.
Update the ESP32 UART bridge and JSON UDP relay.
Update the DAQ UDP connection and start logic.
Open the serial monitor for ESP32 and Teensy, then press connect in the DAQ GUI.
validation_steps: Confirm ESP32 receives HELLO and replies READY.
Confirm ESP32 prints [ESP32] Teensy RX: TLM|....
Confirm DAQ prints telemetry packet received and gauge values update.
Confirm stop works and the Teensy stops emitting telemetry.
final_goal: The final system must behave as a simple and stable telemetry bridge: DAQ sends command over Wi‑Fi UDP to ESP32; ESP32 forwards to Teensy over UART; Teensy emits telemetry; ESP32 forwards JSON back to the DAQ; DAQ updates gauges; no unnecessary startup loops or simulator logic.
